findings.title: latticeignoreweights freezes the lattice bins on bootstrap()'s count leg and under bayes
findings.claim: The count leg carries each bootstrap replicate as [aw=basew*draw], and bayes carries the Dirichlet mass the same way. latticeignoreweights strips that weight out of the lattice quantiles, so every replicate reuses the original sample's bins. The re-id leg rebuilds the bins on the resample. The bootstrap SE therefore depends on which leg the engine picks, and on unweighted data an option that does nothing analytically changes the bootstrap result.
findings.evidence: D.do on dta_cont with no user weights: wooldid y i t ttre, contreat(intensity) contreatcontrols(basic) cluster(i) lattice(all 2) [latticeignoreweights] bootstrap(standard) reps(20) rseed(1). Re-id leg (att att_it): .00351941787324 / .0108026659989 with and without LIW. rseed is fixed in all four runs, so the count leg without LIW matching the re-id leg to 12 digits while the LIW count-leg value differs is a code-path difference, not Monte-Carlo noise. findings.title: unconditionalse scales the whole linearized variance by regress's (N-1)/(N-K), with K counting every cell and i dummy
findings.claim: The unconditionalse SE is exactly Stata's margins vce(unconditional) after regress.
